text: This lesson goes deep into actually reading an execution plan — the direction data flows, what the icons mean, what arrow thickness tells you, and how cost percentages should and shouldn't guide where you look first.

Plans read backwards from English. The rightmost, bottom-most operator runs first — usually table or index access. Data flows left and up until it reaches SELECT on the far left, the final result handed back to the client.

Index Seek means the engine navigated the B-tree directly — efficient. A Scan reads every row, fine on a small table but a flag at scale. A Key Lookup is an extra trip to the clustered index per matching row. Hash Match and Nested Loops are how two inputs actually get joined.

Arrow thickness encodes row count flowing between operators, not cost. Cost percentage is the optimizer's own estimate of relative cost within this one plan — a great lead, but not proof, and it can be flatly wrong.

A thick arrow that barely thins on its way to SELECT usually means a WHERE clause isn't filtering as effectively as you'd expect. Next up: what happens when the optimizer's estimate and the real, actual numbers disagree.
